newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-STARS BEAT RED WINGS FOR LEAGUE-BEST SIXTH VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-STARS BEAT RED WINGS FOR LEAGUE-BEST SIXTH VICTORY.

text.p: The surprising Dallas Stars just keep on winning with the high-powered Detroit Red Wings their latest victims.
Jere Lehtinen and Sergei Zubov scored 17 seconds apart in the second period and Arturs Irbe made 32 saves as the Stars skated to a 3-1 victory Tuesday, their sixth in as many games.
Guy Carbonneau added a goal and an assist for the Stars, who have outscored their opponents 23-11 and are off to their best start in franchise history, a league-best 6-0-0.
Irbe allowed only Darren McCarty's goal at 9:09 of the first period. Dallas responded with three second-period goals, ending an 11-game winless streak against Detroit.
"It's not hard to play behind a defence like that," Irbe said. "The defence and forwards gave me a clear look at a lot of shots and I even had a second to recover on deflections."
Lehtinen deflected Derian Hatcher's wrist shot from the top of the right faceoff circle past Mike Vernon at 7:12 of the second.

Seventeen seconds later Zubov, who was acquired from Pittsburgh in the off-season, broke a 1-1 deadlock by firing a wrist shot from the blue line over Vernon's left shoulder for his first goal for Dallas.
Guy Carbonneau completed the scoring just over seven minutes later.
"It's special to come away with a win like that against one of the top teams," Irbe said.

The loss was a costly one for Detroit. Steve Yzerman left the game in the third period after getting hit in the face with a stick. Tim Taylor went out in the first with a shoulder injury and Igor Larionov left with a groin injury.
At Colorado, Eric Lacroix recorded his first NHL hat trick and Joe Sakic had a career-high six points on a goal and five assists as the Avalanche buried the Edmonton Oilers 7-2.
Sandis Ozolinsh scored 56 seconds into the game and added two assists for the defending Stanley Cup champions, who stretched their unbeaten streak to four games.
Peter Forsberg and Valeri Kamensky scored third-period Colorado goals, each setting up the other.

Lacroix, the son of Colorado General Manager Pierre Lacroix, scored at 7:25 when he backhanded a rebound of Ozolinsh's shot past goaltender Curtis Joseph. He scored again at 8:48 of the second and completed the hat trick with his fifth goal of the season at 14:05 for a 5-1 lead.
At Buffalo, Dino Ciccarelli scored twice and Corey Schwab turned aside 22 shots for his first NHL shutout as the Tampa Bay Lightning blanked the Sabres 4-0.
Schwab faced just six shots in the second period and seven in the third from an anaemic Buffalo attack that has scored only three goals in its last four games.
Ciccarelli re-directed a Chris Gratton slap shot past goalie Dominik Hasek on a powerplay at 11:15 of the first period. He doubled the lead at 4:18 of the second.
Drew Bannister and Jason Wiemer each picked up their first goal of the season to complete the scoring.
At New Jersey, Valeri Zelepukin had a goal and two assists and Martin Brodeur made 28 saves as the Devils held on for a 3-2 victory over the Montreal Canadiens.

Zelepukin scored on a breakaway at 16:20 of the first period, beating Jocelyn Thibault with a slap shot. He assisted on goals by Sergei Brylin in the second period and Bill Guerin midway through the third as the Devils built a 3-0 lead.

Brodeur's shutout bid evaporated 91 seconds later as Montreal struck twice in a 16-second span on goals by Saku Koivu and Vincent Damphousse. But Montreal could not come up with the equaliser and suffered its first loss of the season.
In Toronto, Kevin Miller snapped a tie 7:49 into the third period and Ed Belfour made 39 saves as the Chicago Blackhawks ended a three-game slide with a 3-1 win over the Maple Leafs.
Miller took a pass from James Black and fired a slap shot over Felix Potvin's glove for his first goal as a Blackhawk.
Kirk Muller scored a short-handed goal for Toronto 2:43 into the game but Belfour shut the Leafs down the rest of the way, making 21 saves in the third period alone.
Tony Amonte scored the other two Chicago goals, tying the game at 13:35 of the first period and sealing the win on an empty net goal with 42 seconds left.
In Los Angeles, the Kings came up with a powerplay goal, a short-handed tally and an even strength goal in the second period to edge the Philadelphia Flyers 3-2.
After Pat Falloon's first-period goal put the Flyers up 1-0, Kevin Stevens put a backhander past goaltender Garth Snow on the powerplay at 8:10 of the second to even the score.
The Kings took the lead 89 seconds later with Philadelphia on a powerplay when Jaroslav Modry ripped a slap shot by Snow.
Brent Grieve notched the game-winner when his shot from the right corner hit Flyers defenceman Karl Dykhuis and deflected into the Philadelphia goal.
